questions.prompt: Explain why atoms of the same element can have different mass numbers. (3)

questions.prompt: Explain why ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten but not when solid. (4)
hints: Compare ion mobility in solid and liquid states.
questions.solution:
Ionic compounds contain charged ions. [B1]
In a solid lattice the ions are fixed in position and cannot move. [B1]
When molten the ions are free to move. [B1]

questions.inspiredBy: AQA 8462 Chemistry Paper 1 style · Bonding, structure, and the properties of matter · family 1

questions.prompt: Explain why graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not. (4)
hints: How many bonds does each carbon make?
questions.solution:
Both are giant covalent forms of carbon. [B1]
In graphite each carbon forms three covalent bonds, leaving one delocalised electron per carbon. [B1]
The delocalised electrons can move and carry charge. [B1]
In diamond each carbon forms four covalent bonds so there are no free electrons or ions to carry charge. [B1]
questions.inspiredBy: AQA 8462 Chemistry Paper 1 style · Bonding, structure, and the properties of matter · family 2

questions.prompt: Explain why metals are malleable and conduct electricity. (4)

Layers of metal ions can slide past one another while metallic bonding is maintained, so the metal is malleable. [B1]
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the structure. [B1]
The moving electrons carry electrical charge. [B1]
